title: IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics
seo_title: IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics | Dataq Software
meta_description: IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics services from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: The physical floor, mirrored live — twins and robotics programs that lift OEE, cut unplanned downtime and prove it on your own telemetry.

IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge AI, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. The tower's test is operational: fewer unplanned stoppages, tighter quality distributions, safer floors, and asset performance you can steer from a control tower.

Compute moved to the plant floor and the camera moved into the process. Vision models now read gauges and weld seams; twins simulate line reconfiguration before steel is cut; retrofitted robots pay back in under two years against labor scarcity. Physics-heavy industries that industrialized this stack are compounding an operational advantage that software-only competitors cannot copy.

items: Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.
Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.
Cameras into instruments: inspection, safety and counting at the edge, inside policy.
Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Robots into workflows: AMRs, cobots and autonomous vehicles integrated with safety and orchestration.
Your product becomes a service: device fleets, OTA and telemetry products with revenue attached.
Facilities that run themselves: BMS/IoT fusion, energy optimization and city-scale platforms.

blocks.x: Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus carry the production rails for this tower — governance, security posture and audit evidence production are inherited from the platform, so programs harden instead of improvising.

items: Critical assets instrumented within agreed quarters
Line/capacity decisions simulated in hours, not shutdown windows

blocks.x: Anchor industries: Agriculture & Food Systems, Education & Research, Energy & Utilities, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Logistics & Supply Chain, Manufacturing & Industrial, Public Sector & Government, Retail & Consumer Goods, Telecom, Media & Entertainment.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
At the end of the first quarter of a typical program you hold four concrete assets:

items: The signed measurement of where the metric stands today, with the method written out so the number can be defended to finance.
Every automated decision path, its policy checks, its human checkpoint and its owner on one page.
Logs, evaluations and approvals collected automatically as the program runs — ready for internal audit or a regulator.
A running record of the delta against baseline, updated at every gate, reviewed at every steering meeting.
